clue.text: Mine are reserves of bread

parts.note: a mine is a pit dug for coal or ore
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: Someone claims their stockpiles of loaves are personal property.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitta is a flat, pocketed Middle Eastern loaf, a kind of bread.

clue.text: Self-professed dignitary may censure Jan for tattoo

parts.note: to pan is to criticise harshly, as a reviewer might
taken as written
a tattoo is a drumbeat, such as an evening signal on a drum

explanation.surface: A pompous official might rebuke a man called Jan for getting inked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tattoo' tempts as body art, but here it is the military drumbeat; 'may' and 'for' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A pompous person who thinks of themselves as an important official is mockingly called this.

clue.text: Double support for two-engined plane

parts.note: twin means double, paired
a prop is a support holding something up

explanation.surface: Something giving twice the backing to an aircraft with two engines.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft with two propeller-driven engines is called by this name.

clue.text: The beano era adapted to such an organism

indicators.note: something adapted has been changed in form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A party era changed into a kind of living thing.
explanation.walkthrough: BEANO is British slang for a party or celebration; 'The' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: An organism that lives without oxygen is one adapted to such conditions, so the clue's era shapes it.

clue.text: Took control and fires the rifles

parts.note: to run something, past tense ran, is to be in charge of it
to fire an employee is to sack them

explanation.surface: A commander seized power and discharged the guns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rifles' looks like guns, but it is the verb meaning to search and plunder.
explanation.definitionFit: To rifle a place is to search it thoroughly and steal from it, i.e. plunder.

clue.text: Rose called for her eggs

indicators.note: something called out is spoken, so the name is heard rather than seen

parts.note: taken as written, the girl's name or flower

explanation.surface: A woman named Rose asks for her breakfast eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: Roe is the mass of eggs carried by a female fish.

clue.text: Cavils are wrong to denounce Slavonic language

indicators.note: letters that are wrong are out of order, so the word is rearranged

explanation.surface: Petty objections are mistaken when used to attack an Eastern European tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to denounce' is surface padding joining the parts.
explanation.definitionFit: The family of tongues spoken across eastern Europe, including Russian and Polish, goes by this name.

clue.text: Angle somewhat banal for the queen

indicators.note: somewhat says only part of the word is used, its end dropped

parts.note: corny means trite or banal
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the queen

explanation.surface: A rather trite viewpoint offered on behalf of the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A corner is a place where two lines or walls meet at an angle.

clue.text: Sound profit made from watch, right

definitions.note: profit sounds like prophet, a person who foretells the future

parts.note: to watch is to see

explanation.surface: Solid gains earned from a timepiece, correctly.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a sound-alike: 'profit' is heard as prophet.
explanation.definitionFit: A prophet is one who foresees events, a visionary.

clue.text: Pain is in a subtle difference

indicators.note: one word is placed in the other

parts.note: a nuance is a slight shade of difference

explanation.surface: Suffering lies in a fine distinction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pain' is the colloquial sense: an annoying person or thing.
explanation.definitionFit: A pain, colloquially, is an annoyance, something irritating.

clue.text: Reminder I am nervous about reformation

indicators.note: a reformation reshapes something, so these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone admits being anxious about religious reform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'am' is a link word; the anagram uses I and NERVOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: A keepsake bought on holiday serves as a memento of the trip.

clue.text: Strange is the tie I wear from quirks

parts.note: odd means strange

indicators.note: the outer word is pictured wearing the inner one around it

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone finds their own necktie unusual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wear' signals a container: the short word is pictured wearing the tie around the neck. 'the' and 'I' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Peculiarities or eccentric traits are oddities.

clue.text: Hoping to detail pain killer

indicators.note: to de-tail is to remove a word's last letter

parts.note: aspiring means hoping to achieve something

explanation.surface: Someone hopes to describe the drug in detail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detail' looks like 'describe fully'; read as de-tail, it cuts off the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A common analgesic tablet relieves headaches and aches.

clue.text: Skittles make one cross legs

parts.note: one is I and a cross is X, giving IX, the Roman numeral for nine
pins is slang for legs

explanation.surface: A party game makes a player cross their legs.
explanation.walkthrough: PINS is informal British for legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Ninepins is an old bowling game in which a ball knocks down skittles.

clue.text: Impropriety in wrong code — strange

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: letters set wrong are in the wrong order, so the word is rearranged

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd or strange

explanation.surface: Misconduct involving a faulty and odd code.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' makes DECO from CODE.
explanation.definitionFit: Indecorum is unseemly behaviour, a lack of propriety.

clue.text: Bewitches me twice round the section's the lifts

indicators.note: the doubled word goes round the abbreviation
twice means the word is written two times over

parts.note: taken as written
S is a short form of section
rises means lifts up

explanation.surface: A doubled self circling a passage puts a spell on lifts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twice' gives MEME, and 'round' puts S inside it to make MESME.
explanation.definitionFit: To mesmerise is to hypnotise or enthral, as if under a spell.

clue.text: Striptease never changes salesmen

indicators.note: the fodder letters undergo changes into a new order

explanation.surface: A stripper never alters the routine for the travelling salesmen.
explanation.definitionFit: Sales reps travel selling a company's goods to customers.

clue.text: Divinity is the subject of study

parts.note: taken as written
an ology is informally any branch of learning

explanation.surface: Religion is a branch of academic study.
explanation.definitionFit: Divinity, as a university subject, is the study of God and religion.

clue.text: Green laic crooked yet upright

parts.note: vert is the heraldic word for green

indicators.note: crooked means bent out of line, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An environmentally minded lay person is bent, yet standing tall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crooked' makes ICAL from LAIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Something upright stands straight up, perpendicular to the horizon.

clue.text: Manly Sam upset with copper spiel

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a line is a patter or sales spiel

explanation.surface: Sam is annoyed by a policeman's patter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' makes MAS from SAM; 'copper' tempts as a policeman.
explanation.definitionFit: Manly behaviour has qualities traditionally associated with men.

clue.text: Master performance of little runner

indicators.note: a performance of a piece reworks it, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A skilled performer's show featuring a small athlete.
explanation.definitionFit: A brook or small river is a narrow course of running water.

clue.text: Not rough cut peace keepers when wrong

parts.note: UN peacekeeping forces are United Nations troops

indicators.note: letters gone wrong are out of order, so the word is rearranged

explanation.surface: Peacekeeping troops are hardly rough when they get it wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' makes HEWN from WHEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Stone or timber not shaped with an axe or chisel remains in its natural state.

clue.text: Vehicle used to score

indicators.note: letters used up are worked into something else, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A car employed in order to win points.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used' is an unusual anagram signal, meaning the letters are put to use in another form.
explanation.definitionFit: A scooter is a light motorcycle or a child's kick-propelled ride.

clue.text: Leverage into having to buy

explanation.surface: Gaining influence by being forced to acquire something.
explanation.definitionFit: Purchase means a firm grip giving mechanical advantage, and as a verb it means acquiring by payment.

clue.text: If tipped I am flat out

indicators.note: the outer word sits out around the inner letter

parts.note: a pad is slang for a flat or apartment
taken as written

explanation.surface: Being toppled leaves someone lying flat on the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tipped' looks like toppled; here it means given a gratuity. 'If' and 'am' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A waiter who has been tipped has been given extra money.

clue.text: Cut tail off snake over Icelandic books

indicators.note: over in a down clue turns the word upside down, reading it backwards
cutting the tail off removes a word's last letter

parts.note: an adder is a venomous snake

explanation.surface: Instructions for docking a serpent written over Norse texts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut tail off' leaves ADDE, and 'over' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: The Eddas are two medieval Icelandic collections of Norse myth and poetry.

clue.text: Absolutely split matches

parts.note: matches are marriages, and a decree absolute legally ends a marriage

explanation.surface: Matchsticks broken clean in two.
explanation.walkthrough: 'matches' reads as matchsticks; here they are marriages, ended by a decree absolute in English law.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal ends to marriages are formalised by a final decree.

clue.text: Mad to use dimetane for mental disorder

indicators.note: mad means crazy, so the letters go wild and are rearranged

explanation.surface: It would be crazy to take an antihistamine for a psychiatric illness.
explanation.walkthrough: Dimetane is a brand of antihistamine; 'to use' and 'for' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A progressive decline in memory and thinking is a brain disorder.

clue.text: Barks an uncouth reply and succeeded after king abdicated

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held: 'Barks an uncouth reply and succeeded after king abdicated (5)'. YEP (uncouth reply) + S (succeeded) leaves the L of YELPS unaccounted for, and 'after king abdicated' gives no letter or removal that supplies it; no search found the clue.
annotationWithheld.clue: Barks an uncouth reply and succeeded after king abdicated
